claim: RZ-NAS's official implementation confirms its search procedure is an evolutionary search (evolution_search.py) parameterized by a choice of zero-cost proxy score and search space, not a chain of sequential LLM self-refinement calls each treated as the new baseline.
stance_target: structural comparability between RZ-NAS's positive feedback result and the target paper's sequential-refinement degradation claim
scope_conditions: Official code repository, PasaLab/RZ-NAS on GitHub
quoted_support: One example of the whole prompt is saved in template.txt. More zero-cost proxies and search spaces are saved under the folder descriptions. For different zero-cost proxies, you can change the parameter zero_shot_score.

claim: RZ-NAS prompts combine a role, detailed instructions, an in-context example, and a reflective module, replacing full architecture training with zero-cost proxies to reduce compute cost while retaining competitive performance, per the method's own description.
stance_target: mechanism by which RZ-NAS's LLM feedback loop is made computationally cheap and structured, distinguishing it from unstructured chat-based self-refinement
scope_conditions: Official README, RZ-NAS ICML 2025 code release
quoted_support: We rethink LLMs' roles in NAS in current work and design a structured, prompt-based to comprehensively understand the search task and architectures from both text and code levels.
